**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 13.4.1 already delivers our preferred position on the material terms:
- **Customer assignment freedom:** AbbVie may assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction of the business to which the Agreement relates.
- **Consent standard:** any other assignment requires the other Party's consent, "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" — and the restriction is symmetrical, so Harpoon is equally bound.
- **No change-of-control exit for the Vendor:** the only change-of-control provisions run in our favour — Section 13.2 obliges Harpoon to notify us of a Change in Control of Harpoon, and Sections 2 (p0273) and 5 (p0369) give AbbVie additional rights where a Competitor acquires Harpoon. Nothing gives Harpoon a termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie change of control, so walk-away territory is not engaged.

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: the clause has no express bar on Harpoon assigning to an AbbVie competitor, and the consent requirement is mutual rather than one-way — both minor sub-elements against a bargain that is otherwise at or above the preferred position.
